Zuma vs Zondo - The Standoff

By: Sophia Phirippides | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Former President Zuma is refusing to return to the Zondo Commission even under order of the Constitutional Court. Is this the endgame for Zuma versus Zondo, finally?

Unique Selling Point:
On 28 January 2021 The Constitutional Court of South Africa directed Mr Jacob Gedleyihlekisa Zuma "to appear and give evidence before the [ Zondo ] Commission on dates determined by it".

Four days later, on 01 February 2021, Mr Jacob Gedleyihlekisa Zuma released a statement declaring "in advance that the Commission Into Allegations of State Capture can expect no further co-operation from me in any of their processes going forward. If this stance is considered to be a violation of their law, then let their law take its course."

The long running standoff between the Zondo Commission and former President Jacob Zuma, who set up the commission, appears to be reaching a head and on 15 February 2021 we will find out if Zuma follows through with his defiance and if the judiciary follow through with the Law.

Zuma claims he is being victimized by the State, harking back to Apartheid judicial practices that targetted specific individuals. With his defiance of the Constitution and the Zondo Commission, can Zuma avoid jail for contempt of court or does he even want to?

For now the ball is in Zuma's court but depending on how he plays it, who has more to gain and lose in the endgame? The 26 year old fledgeling democracy of South Africa or the 78 year old former statesman Jacob Zuma?

Press Release:


It’s the endgame in the long running standoff between the Zondo Commission and former President Jacob Zuma, as Zuma has threatened to defy the Zondo Commission and the Constitution. Who has more to lose? The seventy eight year old former statesman or the twenty six year old democracy of South Africa?

Script:


Zuma: The interview now it’s the wrong time hahaha
Derek: Ok, but then I'll ask you will you be back?
Zuma: I will be back. Derek: You will be back? Ok great. Much LOLs


VO: That was the assurance of former President Jacob Zuma, after testifying before the Commission of Inquiry into State Capture in July 2019. His appeal to Judge Zondo to allow him time to review evidence before continuing testimony had been granted.


Zuma: I’m sure that adds the confidence we have on you as a Chair,
Zondo: and the former President will come back at another time that will be arranged.


VO: But that was then...


LINK: After numerous attempts by the Zondo Commission to try and get former President Jacob Zuma to complete his testimony, he finally made an appearance in November last year // only to walk out of the proceedings// leading to a summons to appear. Now the highest court in the land has ruled that Zuma must face the commission - he says, andizi, I’m not coming and I’m willing to go to jail.


Richard: it's a very important moment. It's a serious moment, a grave moment even.


VO: Richard Calland, Associate Professor of Public Law at UCT, maintains that the former president is compelled to adhere to the law as ordered by Justice Jafta.


Richard: Here you have the former president of South Africa threatening to defy an order of the Constitutional Court, who have said that he has flouted the law in the past. He is a pivotal witness for that process. And they've said that he must respect the summons that have been issued.


VO: In a statement on the 1st of February, Jacob Zuma slated the ConCourt and warned that “a politicized segment of the judiciary now heralds an imminent constitutional crisis”. Political Analyst Aubrey Matshiqi is not surprised by Zuma's about turn.


Aubrey: If you look at what he has done and said over the past 15 years, there is enough to alert us to the possibility that he would defy the Zondo Commission. Now, here's the problem. He says the judiciary, not just the commission, is biased.


VO: At the commission in 2019 Zuma positioned himself as a target of conspiracy and threatened to tell all.


Aubrey: You may be dealing here with a man who may be suffering from what I call the Samson complex.he is a man who will have no qualms about pulling down the pillars of the temple with us and our democracy underneath.


VO: The irony is that it was former President Jacob Zuma, who originally set up the commission into state capture on the former Public Protector's recommendation. // But now that he has to testify as an ordinary citizen, he's moved the goalposts and refuses to appear on the 15th of February, unless Judge Raymond Zondo recuses himself.


Zondo: We return to the hearing in circumstances where Mr Zuma has left.


Pierre: in a case where there's a commission of inquiry, it is very difficult to have somebody removed for a conflict of interest He has not provided any serious evidence that will show that there is a real likelihood or real fear that Judge Zondo will be biased.


VO: According to Professor in Constitutional law at UCT, Pierre de Vos, this could be another strategic move by Zuma.


Pierre: Legally speaking, you would think you would want to go and give your version of events. You have nothing to lose unless of course, you lie and you are later prosecuted and the lies come back to bite you. Politically, is what might make it wise because the president is trying to delegitimize the whole state capture commission.


Masa: Is this another delay tactic?
Aubrey: No this is not a delaying tactic. If he goes to jail, that's the end, he will never go back to the commission. And that's what he wants, in my view.


VO: And the penalties seem rather paltry: For contempt of court, Zuma could be fined, or jailed for up to six months, or both. He could also be prosecuted in terms of the Commission's Act with a maximum sentence of six months.


Aubrey: The optics of Jacob Zuma being arrested, serving sentence have political implications.


LINK: Zuma says he has overwhelming support within his party, the ANC and outside of it. A structure of the ANC, the MKMVA, has threatened Civil War should he be arrested.


Richard :So within the ANC, there's no doubt that Mr. Zuma still enjoys some support, but it is my view, dwindling.The idea that Mr. Zuma can turn the ANC around and impose himself upon it, I think is entirely misconceived.


Masa: What do you make of President Cyril Ramaphosa’s silence?
Aubrey:There is an extent to which he is seen as a foe to be former president, and also a foe to the Secretary General Ace Magashule.there is a possibility that the Zuma matter and the Magashule matter may intersect to the detriment of political stability inside and outside the ANC.


LINK: When Secretary General Ace Magashule was ambushed by media this week to respond to the former president's behaviour, he didn't mince his words.


Ace: What is the problem here, what has Zuma done now?
Reporter: There are calls now for him to be suspended - will the ANC entertain that?
Ace: No - Why should we suspend a person who believes in what he believes in? Pres Zuma has the right to do whatever he wants to do.


VO: Even though Magashule emphasised the NEC had yet to discuss the matter, did his words set a tone, for everyone in the firing line for wrongdoing? He too is facing charges for alleged corruption.
ANC's spokesperson Pule Mabe joined us online to clarify the ANC's position.


Masa: Should the Constitutional's Court ruling be upheld?
Pule: All constitutional court rulings should always be upheld. The constitutional court is the highest court in the land.
Masa: Your Secretary General says not what you're saying. He says Zuma must be left alone and he's done nothing wrong. So who are we to listen to?
Pule: It is not about who we are to listen to. I think the ANC speaks, it speaks in one voice. So something unfortunate happened, I mean, we were visiting Ma Kotane’s family to go and convey our condolences. So to be ambushed outside the gate of a grieving family was rather unfortunate. but these journalists insisted.
Masa: The journalists insisted, you're correct but they didn't make your SG say what he said.
Pule: I'm answering your question in the manner I did it
Masa: Okay Pule. My apologies, you may continue.
Pule: You are disturbing my train of thought. That's what happened to the SG. When he was busy trying to answer journalists, then they come in "Do you think Zuma is right? What must happen to Zuma?". You ask a person seven questions at once. We are human beings, we are not machines. Journalists just mobbed us.
So it's rather unfortunate, and we do take responsibility that perhaps the message that went out there was not a very pleasant one. But this is not a reflection of the ANC position or the views of the Secretary General. The SG of the ANC respects the constitution.


VO: The ANC stance is clear, that only once their NEC has met in mid February, will they state their official position on the Zuma issue.


Pule: And we will still make an appeal to the former president of the ANC to work with all of us in making sure that the respect of the constitution of this country as the supreme law of the land is upheld by all of us.


Richard: Very serious issues have been raised, involving billions of Rand potentially stolen from the public purse, Mr. Zuma has been asked to give his version of events - he's refusing - that's at the heart of what this is all about.
